title: llm-routing-and-fallback-scratchpad
content:
(personal scratchpad) rough PRD outline + user stories + idea parking lot for LLM routing, variant fallback, and cheap-path routing. Mostly thinking aloud - messy, TODOs, questions for follow-up.

Context:
- Product need: applications using Redwood want predictable latency/cost while preserving output quality. We already have model variants (full, quantized, distilled) and region/capacity tiers. Need a unified policy/routing layer that decides: route to fast/cheap variant vs high-quality variant, when to fallback, and how to surface degradations to app.
- Current infra: smart routing exists but limited to hard-coded rules per-customer. No per-request quality budget or automated decisioning based on prompt characteristics.

Problem statement (short):
- Customers want a single lightweight control to trade cost/latency vs quality per route. Also need robust fallbacks when the chosen variant fails or quality degrades.

Goals / success metrics (ideas):
- Reduce average per-token inference cost for eligible routes by 20% within 3 months of rollout (metric: $cost/token by route).
- Maintain user-perceived quality: >95% of sampled prompts show no regression against baseline (quality eval set).
- P99 latency target preserved for routes configured with latency SLOs.
- Fallback coverage: automatic fallback triggers correctly in >98% of simulated failure cases.

Constraints & assumptions:
- Model variants must be compatible for semantic equivalence checks (we have eval harness).
- We can access simple prompt metadata (length, tokens, endpoint, user-tier) but not full app context for every request.
- Can't add >20ms median overhead in routing decision. Must be async or cached where possible.

Feature ideas (brain dump):
1) Per-route quality budget: user sets "quality_score_floor" e.g., 0.9 (0..1) and a cost goal. Router routes to cheap variant only when estimated quality >= floor.
   - Estimator: small classifier that predicts probability cheap variant will pass quality for this prompt (based on prompt embeddings + length + recent drift signals).
   - Fall back to full model if low confidence.
2) Prefix caching + variant reuse: if at prefix time we have cached KV state from full model for this prompt series, prefer using cheaper variant for short completions.
3) Canary rollout for variant routing: roll out cheap-path to X% of traffic with automatic rollback if eval set or online metrics degrade.
4) Multi-tier fallback policy: cheap -> mid -> full. Allow policy weights and thresholds, and per-customer overrides.
5) Graceful degradation responses: annotate response metadata with "served_variant" and "fallback_reason" so apps can surface notifications.
6) Quality probes: run async golden-checks on subset of requests by re-running later on full model and compare; store diffs for regression alerts.

User stories (rough):
- As a Growth PM, I want to enable a cost-optimized variant for non-critical content generation so that we reduce billable tokens without breaking UX.
- As an App engineer, I want to know which variant served each response so I can log and A/B my product logic.
- As a SRE, I want automated fallback when capacity or model error rate increases so customer-facing latency doesn't spike.
- As an ML engineer, I want to evaluate the cheap-path predictor performance on historical prompts before rollout.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Estimator cost: can we run a cheap classifier per-request with <20ms? Possibly use a cached embedding + fast logistic model on CPU. Need perf experiment (ask infra).
- What feature set for estimator? Prompt embedding, token length, user tier, recent perf of the variant, prompt namespace? Privacy implications for storing embeddings? (Data/privacy check needed).
- How to label training data: use historical pairs (cheap_variant output vs full model) and compute pass/fail on eval rubric. Need dataset size estimate.
- Mutation semantics: when fallback re-runs on full model, do we return full-model text synchronously (higher latency) or return cheap result + async patch? Both have UX tradeoffs.
- Billing semantics: if we fall back to full model, do we bill full usage or offer blended price? (commercial/legal).

Risks / failure modes:
- Regressions: cheap variant introduces subtle quality regressions not captured by short eval sets. Mitigation: expand evals, holdback sets, human review for early rollouts.
- Exploits: adversarial prompts that trick estimator into preferring cheap path. Add adversarial training and rate limit unknown prompts.
- Monitoring noise: frequent fallbacks generate noisy signals. Build smoothing and minimum window before toggling.

Minimal viable scope (MVP) proposal:
- Implement simple per-route policy: allow customer to enable "cheap_path" boolean with two knobs: "max_cheap_pct" and "quality_budget_score".
- Build a lightweight estimator prototype (embedding + logistic) offline and run in replay to measure precision/recall.
- Add metadata in response: served_variant and fallback_flag.
- Add a canary rollout + manual rollback.

Phased roadmap (sketch):
- Week 0-2: alignment doc + proto estimator offline replay (ML team).
- Week 3-6: runtime support for per-route policy, response metadata, config UI in Console (product + console).
- Week 7-10: canary rollout, quality probes, alerting.
- Month 3: expand to multi-tier policies and automatic rollback heuristics.

Open TODOs (my personal):
- [ ] Create replay dataset and label heuristics (ask applied-ml for dataset and eval rubric). -> TODO: @Maya Li to share eval script references (Slack thread #applied-ml).
- [ ] Spike on estimator latency on a t2.medium CPU instance (ask infra).
- [ ] Draft API shape for per-route policy (route config + fallback policy). Rough idea below.

Rough API (informal):
- route_config: {"cheap_path_enabled": true, "quality_budget": 0.92, "max_cheap_pct": 0.2, "fallback_policy": ["cheap","mid","full"]}
- response metadata: served_variant: "quant-8bit", fallback_reason: "estimator_low_confidence", routing_decision_score: "0.73"

Notes to self / meeting agenda items:
- Review with Applied ML: dataset + labeling strategy.
- Sync with Infra on estimator runtime constraints and cost.
- Check Console UX: where to surface served_variant and fallback notifications.
- Legal: billing semantics on fallbacks.

Related links + references:
- PLAT-4321: model-variant-routing (jira)
- Confluence: LLM Routing Design (linked above)
- PR: serving-runtime #829 (kernel for variant tagging)
- Slack: #product-hosted-api thread "cheap-path routing" (search)

End of scratchpad. Will clean up into a formal PRD once experiments (replay + latency) return promising signals.

-- Samira
